TCV #85604 · Hermes-3 simulation · 20 November 2026

Camera to divertor heat, on frames the model has never seen

A synthetic gas-puff camera looks at the outer midplane. From its frames alone the model predicts the heat flux reaching the outer divertor target. In between it estimates the slow state (the toroidally averaged part of the model's internal state), adds a toroidal pattern drawn from training frames, and turns both into the fields at the target with a frozen pretrained decoder and a small refiner on the target rows. Heat is computed from those fields with the sheath formula and is used only for scoring.

The camera alone follows target heat on frames no part of the model has seen

Error 3.0 kW/m² for electron and 1.6 kW/m² for ion heat, against a simulation mean of 87.0 ± 5.1 and 86.5 ± 4.8 kW/m². Dashed lines are forecasts made from camera frames 42 μs earlier.

The heat profile along the target is reproduced within 2.2% and 3.7%

Time-mean heat flux along the outer target on the unseen frames. Peaks 454 against 448 kW/m² for electrons and 193 against 193 kW/m² for ions.

Ion heat can be forecast 42 μs ahead; electron heat cannot

R² is the share of the heat variation captured: 1 is perfect, 0 is no better than always predicting the mean. Dotted lines show the model fed the true slow state and true pattern, 2.2% and 1.5%.

Electron temperature reaches the target within 8 μs; ion heat follows the midplane 65–70 μs later

Correlation in the simulation itself, toroidal mean, near scrape-off layer (the region just outside the last closed flux surface), variations faster than 1 kHz. Electron heat peaks at zero delay, so forecasting it needs a forecast of the midplane itself.

The loss is in going from the midplane to the slow state of the whole domain, not in the camera or the decoder

Feeding the true midplane fields (the simulated fields in the camera's view) instead of the camera barely helps electron heat (0.60 against 0.57); feeding the true slow state gives 0.94. The camera pipeline follows heat below 5 kHz and loses it above; the resampled pattern matches the true one (0.56 against 0.57), while no pattern drops electron heat to 0.31.

These 489 frames give longer, steadier R² than the 120-frame unseen block, where the true slow state scores 0.86 and 0.93; the two are not directly comparable.

Three changes lifted heat prediction

The refiner (0.18 to 0.64), a pattern resampled from training frames instead of none (0.74 to 0.89), and masked learning of the pretrained encoder (training it to fill in hidden parts of the fields; 1–5 kHz variations). Refiner and pattern measured on six test windows in frames 720–2168, masked learning on frames 1680–2168.

The missing information is spread over the near scrape-off layer, the core edge and the target end; the far scrape-off layer does not matter

Each filled dot gives the model the true slow state in one region only; each open dot gives it the truth everywhere except that region. The outer-target end, the near scrape-off layer and the region inside the separatrix each recover about half of the gap on their own (0.76–0.78, from 0.57). The camera map already predicts the far scrape-off layer well, and that region has no effect on heat.

Extra inputs, right panel: twelve probes on the outer target lift the camera from 0.57 to 0.74; earlier camera frames do not help; nothing moves the 42 μs electron forecast. Frames 1680–2168.

Next

  1. Replace the linear camera map with a learned one aimed at the near scrape-off layer and the target end, where the linear map is weakest.
  2. A learned rollout of the midplane for the electron forecast, since no extra input moves it.
  3. One confirming run on the unseen block for whichever map wins.
Unseen block: frames 2233–2352 (120 frames of 2.61 μs, 313 μs); everything was fitted on frames 0–2168 and no part of the model saw this block. Lever results use six test windows in frames 720–2168, which the camera map and refiner never saw but the pretrained decoder did; the frequency-band comparison and masked-learning results use frames 1680–2168 (camera map trained on 0–1499; the pretrained decoder saw them). Correlations are from the simulation itself (frames 0–2168), not the model; the electron-to-ion heat delay uses the unfiltered series. Heat is area-averaged over the outer target. Jobs 7511586, 7511587 (unseen block), 7511897 (correlations) and 7512593 (region swap and extra inputs; the target probes sit on the scored row, so that result is an upper mark).
